title: Early Warnings Are Saving Lives — But One in Three Countries Still Has None
title_zh: 预警正在挽救生命，但仍有三分之一的国家没有预警系统
source_name: UN News — “From Japan to Rwanda, early warnings are saving lives – but millions remain unprotected” (11 Nov 2026)
summary_zh: 11月11日，联合国秘书长古特雷斯在土耳其安塔利亚举行的COP31气候大会上表示，预警系统正在挽救生命，但仍有数百万人收不到预警，他敦促到2027年底让全球每个人都受到预警系统保护。联合国减灾办公室和世界气象组织的新报告显示，136个国家（占70%）已建立多灾种预警系统；预警完善的国家灾害死亡率低6.1倍。文章介绍了日本海啸疏散约190万人、卢旺达茶农提前防雨等事例，也指出约三分之一国家仍无预警系统，最不发达国家、小岛屿国家和冲突地区差距最大。面对强厄尔尼诺，古特雷斯提出把预警变成长期公共服务、弥补资金与能力缺口等措施。
paragraphs: Early warning systems are saving lives around the world, but millions of people still never receive a warning, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on 11 November. At the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, he urged countries to make sure that every person on Earth is protected by such systems by the end of 2027.

His appeal came as the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) published a new report. It shows that 136 countries, or 70 per cent of the total, now have systems that cover multiple hazards, 17 more than in March 2025. Countries with strong systems have disaster death rates 6.1 times lower than countries with weak ones, and 3.2 times fewer people are affected.

The report gives examples of warnings that worked. When a powerful earthquake struck off Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula in July 2025, the first tsunami threat messages were issued within 10 minutes, and Japan evacuated about 1.9 million people. In Rwanda's Karongi district, a tea farmer was warned through women's cooperatives, text messages, local radio and loudspeakers that heavy rain was expected within 48 hours. This gave her time to protect her fields and store her dried tea leaves before the downpour.

However, around one in three countries still has no early warning system at all. The widest gaps are in the least developed countries, small island states and places affected by conflict. "They did the least to cause the climate crisis, but are being hit first and hardest," Guterres said. He pointed out that some European countries have more weather stations meeting global standards than the whole of Africa, adding: "We cannot warn people about what we cannot see."

A strong El Niño is raising the stakes. The head of the WMO, Celeste Saulo, warned that it "could be literally off our monitoring charts", but said many of its worst human consequences could still be prevented.

Guterres called on governments to make early warnings a permanent public service, close gaps in funding and skills, and replace scattered projects with long-term support for country-led plans. Since 2022, about $2 billion has been raised and around 160 countries are receiving help. Warnings are also increasingly triggering action before disasters strike: in 2025, such "anticipatory action" reached 9.6 million people in 54 countries. "The climate crisis is accelerating," Guterres said. "Our protection of people must accelerate with it."
paragraphs_zh: 联合国秘书长古特雷斯11月11日表示，预警系统正在世界各地挽救生命，但仍有数以百万计的人从未收到过预警。在土耳其安塔利亚举行的第31届联合国气候变化大会（COP31）上，他敦促各国确保到2027年底，地球上的每一个人都能受到这类系统的保护。
在他发出呼吁之际，联合国减少灾害风险办公室（UNDRR）和世界气象组织（WMO）发布了一份新报告。报告显示，目前有136个国家（占总数的70%）已建立覆盖多种灾害的预警系统，比2025年3月多了17个。与预警系统薄弱的国家相比，拥有完善预警系统的国家灾害死亡率低6.1倍，受灾人数也少3.2倍。
报告列举了几个预警奏效的例子。2025年7月，俄罗斯堪察加半岛附近海域发生强烈地震时，首批海啸威胁警报在10分钟内就已发出，日本疏散了约190万人。在卢旺达卡龙吉区，一位茶农通过妇女合作社、手机短信、地方电台和高音喇叭得知，48小时内将有强降雨。这让她有时间在暴雨来临之前保护好自己的田地，并把晒干的茶叶收藏起来。
然而，仍有约三分之一的国家根本没有预警系统。差距最大的是最不发达国家、小岛屿国家以及受冲突影响的地区。古特雷斯说：“它们对气候危机的责任最小，却最先受到冲击，受害也最深。”他指出，一些欧洲国家拥有的符合全球标准的气象站，比整个非洲大陆还多，并补充说：“我们看不见的东西，就无法向人们发出预警。”
一场强厄尔尼诺现象正在加大风险。世界气象组织秘书长塞莱斯特·绍洛警告说，这次厄尔尼诺“可能真的会超出我们的监测图表范围”，但她也表示，它对人类造成的许多最严重的后果仍然可以避免。
古特雷斯呼吁各国政府把预警变成一项长期的公共服务，弥补资金和能力方面的缺口，并用对各国自主主导的计划的长期支持来取代零散的项目。自2022年以来，已筹集约20亿美元，约160个国家正在获得援助。预警也越来越多地促使人们在灾害发生之前就采取行动：2025年，这类“预先行动”在54个国家惠及960万人。古特雷斯说：“气候危机正在加速，我们对人们的保护也必须随之加快。”

key_words.meaning_zh: n. 危险；灾害（multi-hazard 多灾种的）
adj. 脆弱的；易受伤害的

phrases.meaning_zh: 在他发出呼吁之际（as 表示“正当……的时候”）
比……低6.1倍（指约为对方的六分之一）
最先而且最严重地（受到冲击）

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Early warning systems are now available to every person on Earth.
Early warnings are clearly saving lives, but many vulnerable countries still lack them, so the UN wants everyone covered by 2027.
Japan has the best weather stations in the world.
El Niño cannot cause any serious damage if countries build more roads.
questions.explanation: 全文先说预警系统在挽救生命，再用报告数据和事例证明其效果，接着指出约三分之一国家仍无预警系统，最后介绍古特雷斯提出的措施和2027年目标。B 概括了全文。A 与“数以百万计的人仍收不到预警”相矛盾；C、D 文中没有提到。

evidence.quote: Early warning systems are saving lives around the world, but millions of people still never receive a warning

questions.prompt: According to the new report, how many countries now have multi-hazard early warning systems?
questions.explanation: 第2段写明，136个国家（占总数的70%）已建立覆盖多种灾害的预警系统。17是比2025年3月新增的数量，54是2025年开展预先行动的国家数，160是正在获得援助的国家数。

evidence.quote: 136 countries, or 70 per cent of the total, now have systems that cover multiple hazards

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from Guterres's remark that "We cannot warn people about what we cannot see"?
options: Africa needs more weather stations that meet global standards so that dangers can be detected and warned about.
European countries should close some of their weather stations.
Weather forecasts are not useful for protecting people.
People in Africa do not want to receive warnings.
questions.explanation: 古特雷斯先对比说一些欧洲国家符合全球标准的气象站比整个非洲还多，再说“看不见的东西就无法预警”。由此可推断：非洲缺乏观测能力，需要更多合格气象站才能发现危险并发出预警。B、C、D 都与原文意思相反或无依据。

evidence.quote: He pointed out that some European countries have more weather stations meeting global standards than the whole of Africa
